This integration brings the [Open Plantbook](https://open.plantbook.io/)
plant database into Gladys: for each of your plants, the **ideal ranges** of
soil moisture, temperature, light and air humidity for its species. Combine them
with your own sensors (soil moisture probe, temperature or light sensor) to know
when a plant needs water, light or a warmer spot.

It runs in the cloud: it needs an Internet connection and a free OpenPlantBook
account.

## What you get

- **One device per plant**, with eight read-only features: the minimum and the
  maximum of soil moisture (%), temperature (°C or °F), light (lux) and air
  humidity (%). You can use them on the dashboard and in scene conditions.
- **Scene triggers**, **scene actions** and **dashboard widgets**, described
  below (Gladys 5.1 or later).

## Get your OpenPlantBook credentials

1. Create a free account on [open.plantbook.io](https://open.plantbook.io/).
2. Open the [API keys](https://open.plantbook.io/apikey/show/) page and generate
   a key: you get a **client ID** and a **client secret**.

## Configuration

1. Open the **Configuration** tab of the integration.
2. Paste the **client ID** and the **client secret**.
3. Click **Test the connection** to check them.
4. Find your plants with the **Search a plant** button: type a common or
   scientific name (`monstera`, `basil`, `rose`...). The answer lists the
   OpenPlantBook ids, such as `monstera deliciosa`.
5. Copy the ids into the **Plants** field, separated by commas (30 plants at
   most), for example `monstera deliciosa, ficus lyrata, ocimum basilicum`.
6. Pick the **language of the plant names** (English, French, German or
   Spanish), the **temperature unit** and, if you wish, the **refresh
   interval** (24 hours by default, the thresholds rarely change).
7. Save, then add the plants from the **Discovery** tab.

The thresholds are kept in a local cache: after a restart, or if
OpenPlantBook is unreachable, the devices keep their last known values.

> Tip: do not put a plant device in a room. The plant devices carry
> temperature and humidity _ranges_, not measurements.

## Actions

- **Test the connection**: checks the credentials.
- **Search a plant**: searches the OpenPlantBook database and lists the ids to
  copy into the **Plants** field.
- **Refresh all plants now**: reads every plant again without waiting for the
  refresh interval.

## Scenes

The integration adds its own cards to the scene editor, under the
**Integrations** category.

### Triggers

- **Plant thresholds updated**: the ideal ranges of a plant were read for the
  first time or changed in OpenPlantBook. Optionally pick the plant. The
  following actions can use `{{triggerEvent.data.plant_name}}`,
  `{{triggerEvent.data.min_soil_moisture}}`, `{{triggerEvent.data.max_temperature}}`
  and the other thresholds.
- **OpenPlantBook sync failed**: reading OpenPlantBook started failing (refused
  credentials, quota reached, unknown plant id, service unreachable). One event
  per failure, not one per attempt. Variables: `reason` and `error`.

### Actions

- **Check a plant's conditions**: compares measurements with the ideal ranges
  of a plant. Fill only the measurements you have; each field accepts a value
  or a scene variable, for example the result of a previous "Get the last
  value of a device" action. The temperature is in the configured unit. It
  returns:
  - `in_range`: true when every measurement is in its ideal range;
  - `status`: `ok`, `too_dry`, `too_wet`, `too_cold`, `too_hot`, `too_dark`,
    `too_bright`, `air_too_dry`, `air_too_humid` or `no_data`;
  - `issues_count`: the number of measurements out of range;
  - `message`: a sentence ready to send, e.g. "Swiss cheese plant: soil too
    dry (8 %, min 15 %)."
- **Get a plant's ideal ranges**: exposes the name, scientific name, category
  and every threshold of a plant to the following actions.
- **Refresh OpenPlantBook data**: reads every plant again now.

### Example: "water me" notification

1. Trigger: every day at 6 pm.
2. Action: get the last value of your soil moisture sensor.
3. Action **Check a plant's conditions**: pick the plant, put the variable of
   the previous step in **Soil moisture**.
4. Condition: `in_range` is false.
5. Action: send a message with the `message` output.

## Dashboard

- **Plant card**: the photo and the four ideal ranges of the plant chosen in
  the widget settings, with a **Refresh** button.
- **My plants**: every followed plant with its photo; tap a plant to see its
  ranges. A **Refresh all** button reads everything again.

## Troubleshooting

- _"OpenPlantBook refused the credentials"_: generate a new key on the API keys
  page and paste both values again.
- _A plant stays without data_: check its id with **Search a plant**; the id is
  the lowercase scientific name.
- _"Too many requests"_: the free API is rate limited. Lower the number of
  plants or raise the refresh interval.
- The integration logs everything it does: check the integration logs from the
  Gladys UI, with `LOG_LEVEL=debug` for the full detail. Secrets are never
  logged.

Plant data and photos come from Open Plantbook (https://open.plantbook.io/),
a community project.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings OpenPlantBook asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Connect to OpenPlantBook | `section` | No | Create a free account on open.plantbook.io, then generate an API key (client ID + client secret) on the API keys page and paste both below. List the plants to follow by their OpenPlantBook id (the scientific name, e.g. monstera deliciosa): the "Search a plant" button below finds them for you. |
| Client ID | `string` | Yes |  |
| Client secret | `secret` | Yes |  |
| Plants | `string` | No | OpenPlantBook ids of your plants, separated by commas (30 at most). One Gladys device is created per plant. |
| Language of the plant names | `select` | No | Common names, device and feature names, and scene messages use this language. |
| Temperature unit | `select` | No |  |
| Refresh interval (hours) | `number` | No | How often the thresholds of each plant are read again. They rarely change: once a day is plenty. |

## How to install OpenPlantBook in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: OpenPlantBook appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/gboulvin/gladys-openplantbook:1.0.1`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/gboulvin/Gladys-Openplantbook](https://github.com/gboulvin/Gladys-Openplantbook).

OpenPlantBook requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

OpenPlantBook is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [gboulvin](https://github.com/gboulvin), not by the Gladys core team.
